title: A Cup for Two
text:
Mia has two cups. One cup is blue. One cup is red.

Her dad comes home. He is tired. Mia puts the blue cup on the table. She puts the red cup next to it.

They sit and drink. Dad smiles. Mia smiles too.

title: The Cat at the Door
text:
A cat sits at the door. It is cold outside.

Sam opens the door. The cat comes in. It looks at Sam, then at a soft chair.

Sam says, "You can sit there." The cat jumps up and closes its eyes. Sam laughs.
subtopic: a cat finds a warm place

title: The Red Hat
text:
Ken has a red hat. He puts it on a chair. Then he goes out.

The wind comes in. The hat falls on the floor.

Ken comes back. He looks at the chair. No hat! His dog is on the floor. The hat is under the dog.

title: The Moon in a Cup
text:
At night, Jo sees the moon in a cup of water.

"Is the moon in my cup?" Jo asks.

Jo moves the cup. The moon moves too. Jo looks up. The moon is in the sky.

"There are two moons!" Jo says. Her little brother laughs.

title: A Duck Comes Back
text:
A small duck walks away from the water. It sees a big tree. It sees a yellow flower.

Then it hears a call. The other ducks are on the water.

The small duck runs back. It jumps in. Now all the ducks swim together.
subtopic: a duck returns to its group

title: A Place at the Table
text:
A new girl comes to class. At lunch, she sits alone.

Nina has an empty chair at her table. She moves the chair and says, "Sit with us."

The girl sits down. She opens her lunch. Nina opens hers. They talk about their food. Soon, they are laughing.

title: Where Is the Key?
text:
Tom cannot find his key. He looks in his bag. No key. He looks on the table. No key.

His sister points to the door.

Tom looks at the door. The key is there! He can go in.

"Thank you," Tom says. His sister smiles.

title: A Door for the Wind
text:
The wind taps on a little door. Tap, tap.

A mouse opens it. "Come in," says the mouse.

The wind comes in and blows a small paper boat across the floor. The mouse runs after it.

"That was fun," says the mouse. The wind taps again.
subtopic: a mouse plays with the wind

title: The Little Fish
text:
A little fish swims near a rock. A big fish swims by.

The little fish moves behind the rock. It waits. The big fish goes away.

Now the little fish comes out. It sees two little fish. They swim together in the sun.

title: The Last Cookie
text:
There is one cookie on the plate. Ali wants it. His sister wants it too.

Ali takes a knife and cuts the cookie in two. He gives one part to his sister.

She says, "Thank you."

Ali says, "We can make more tomorrow." They eat and smile.

title: The Blue Umbrella
text: Rain starts when Emi leaves the shop. She has no umbrella. A man by the door has a big blue one. He says, "We can walk together." They go to the bus stop. Emi stays dry. When the bus comes, she waves. The man waves back.

title: A Bird at the Window
text: A small bird sits by the window. It looks at a bit of bread on the ground. The bird jumps down. It takes the bread and flies to a tree. May looks out. The bird is eating in the tree. May smiles and eats her bread too.

title: The Little Cloud
text: A little cloud goes over a dry field. It sees one small flower. The flower is sad. The cloud stops. A little rain falls. The flower stands up. The cloud moves on. Now the flower has water, and the cloud has a friend to visit.

title: The Wet Marks
text: There are wet marks on the floor. Who came in? Ben looks at the door. It is closed. He looks under the table. There is his dog. The dog is wet from the rain. Ben gets a towel. The dog wags its tail.

title: Lia Takes the Train
text: Lia is on a train for the first time. The houses move past her window. Then she sees trees and a river. Her mother gives her an apple. Lia eats and looks out. At the last stop, she can see the sea. "We are here!" she says.

title: A Note in the Lunch Box
text: Jun opens his lunch box. There is rice, an egg, and a small note. The note says, "Have a good day." Jun reads it two times. At home, he puts a note by his mother's cup. It says, "Have a good day too."

title: The Slow Snail
text: A snail is on a leaf. It moves very slowly. A bird flies over it. A rabbit runs by it. The snail keeps moving. At the end of the day, it is on a new leaf. The new leaf has a big drop of water. The snail stops there.

title: A Star in a Box
text: Nora opens a little box. A tiny star is inside. It gives a soft light. Nora takes the box to her dark room. Now she can see her books. In the morning, she opens the window. The star flies out and up into the sky.

title: The Open Box
text: A box is open under the bed. It was closed last night. Kim looks inside. The little toy car is gone. She looks at the floor. There is a red wheel. She follows it to the door. Her brother is there with the car. "I can fix it," he says.

title: A Map in the Bag
text: Omar wants to see a lake. He puts a map in his bag. At the road, he takes the map out. He goes left, then right. Soon he hears water. The lake is in front of him. He sits on the grass and looks at the blue water.

title: The Warm Soup
text: It is a cold day. Ana puts a pot on the stove. Her son brings two carrots. Ana cuts them and puts them in the pot. They wait and talk. Soon the soup is warm. They sit at the table and eat it together.

title: A Seed in the Pot
text: Leo puts a seed in a pot of soil. He gives it a little water. The next day, he sees only soil. He waits. After many days, a small green leaf comes up. Leo calls his sister. "Look," he says. They both smile at the leaf.
subtopic: waiting for a seed to grow

title: The Sleeping Bell
text: A bell hangs by a small door. No one has used it for years. One day, a mouse pulls the rope. The bell makes a soft sound. A bird comes. Then a cat comes. The mouse says, "Now we can all meet here." The bell rings again.

title: The Light Upstairs
text: The room upstairs is usually empty, but a light is on. Ada walks up slowly. She opens the door. A small lamp is on the floor. Next to it is her father. He is looking for his old book. Ada helps him find it under a chair.
subtopic: a light in the empty room

title: The Red Bus
text: Mina gets on a red bus. She wants to go to the park. The bus goes past a school and a shop. Mina looks for the big tree by the park. There it is. She gets off. Her friend is waiting by the tree with a ball.
subtopic: taking the bus to the park

title: One Empty Seat
text: There is one empty seat at the table. Pat sees a new boy standing by the door. Pat points to the seat. The boy sits down. They do not know what to say at first. Then Pat shows him a funny picture. Both of them laugh.

title: A Puppy in the Rain
text: A puppy runs under a tree when rain begins. Drops fall from the leaves. The puppy is still wet. A woman opens her garden gate. She calls the puppy in. There is a dry place by the door. The puppy lies down and waits for the rain to stop.

title: The Talking Stone
text: Ivy finds a small stone on a path. "Please put me by the river," it says. Ivy looks around. No one is there. She takes the stone to the river. The stone says, "Thank you. I like the sound of the water." Ivy smiles and goes home.

title: Who Took the Apple?
text: An apple is gone from the table. Dad asks, "Who took it?" The children say, "Not me." Then they hear a soft sound under the table. Their dog is there with the apple. It has not eaten it. Dad takes the apple, and the dog gets a hug.

title: The Beach in the Morning
text: Rui goes to the beach early. The sand is cool under his feet. He sees two people walking and a dog running. The sun comes up over the water. Rui sits and watches. He has no work today. He can stay a little longer.
subtopic: an early walk by the sea

title: Sara Finds Her Glove
text: Sara has one glove on her hand. The other is gone. She walks back to the shop. She looks by the door and under a chair. No glove. Outside, a child holds it up. "Is this yours?" the child asks. Sara says, "Yes, thank you!"
subtopic: finding a glove on a walk

title: Two Ants
text: Two ants find a bit of food. One ant pulls it. The food does not move. The second ant comes to help. Now the food moves across the ground. They take it to a small hole. They go in, and the food goes in with them.

title: A Paper Moon
text: A child makes a moon from white paper. She puts it on her wall. At night, the room is dark. She cannot see the paper moon. She turns on her little lamp. Now the moon is bright. "Good night," she says. The moon stays on the wall.

title: The Small Bell
text: A small bell rings in the hall. No one is there. It rings again. Nao opens the front door. A cat is on the step. The cat has a bell on its neck. It moves its head, and the bell rings. Nao laughs and opens the gate.

title: A Room with a View
text: Ella is in a new town. Her room has one small window. She opens it and sees a street, a shop, and a hill. In the morning, she walks up the hill. From there, she can see her room. It looks very small. She smiles.
subtopic: seeing a town from a window

title: A New Plant
text: Noah brings a small plant home. He puts it by the window. Every morning, he gives it a little water. One day, he sees a new leaf. He calls his friend to look. "It likes this window," she says. Noah thinks she is right.

title: The Turtle in the Sun
text: A turtle sits on a warm rock. The sun is on its back. A fish moves in the water below. The turtle watches it. Then a cloud covers the sun. The rock is not warm now. The turtle goes into the water and swims away.

title: The Little Dragon
text: A little dragon is cold. It cannot make a big fire. It can only make one tiny light. A girl sees the light and brings a blanket. She sits with the dragon. The light is small, but the room feels warm. The dragon is happy.
subtopic: a dragon warms a cold room

title: The Blue String
text: A blue string is on the floor. It goes out of the room. Max follows it down the hall. It turns under a door. Max opens the door. His sister is there with a blue ball of string. She is making a small gift for him.

title: The Wrong Stop
text: Tao gets off the bus. This is not his stop. He sees a shop and a small park, but not his house. He looks at the bus sign. The next bus comes soon. Tao gets on. Two stops later, he sees his street and goes home.

title: The Broken Pencil
text: Lee's pencil breaks in class. He looks in his bag. There is no other pencil. His friend puts a short pencil on Lee's desk. "You can use this," she says. Lee writes his answer. After class, he gives the pencil back and says thank you.

title: The Bee and the Flower
text: A bee lands on a yellow flower. It stays for a short time. Then it flies to a white flower. The garden has many flowers, but the bee visits only a few. A child watches from the path. When the bee flies away, the child walks on.

title: The Magic Shoe
text: One shoe by the door can jump. It jumps onto a chair, then onto the table. The other shoe stays on the floor. "Come down," says a boy. The jumping shoe stops. The boy puts both shoes on. Now he can jump too.
subtopic: a shoe takes a little trip

title: A Note on the Door
text: There is a note on the door. It says, "Look under the chair." I look there and find another note. It says, "Look by the window." I go to the window. My friend is outside with two cakes. She waves, and I open the door.
subtopic: reading a note from a friend

title: The Bridge to Town
text: A small bridge goes over a river. On one side is a field. On the other side is a town. Jo walks across with her grandfather. They stop in the middle to look at the water. Then they go to the town and buy bread.

title: Two Tickets
text: Nia has two tickets for a show. She asks her brother to go with her. He says yes. They put on their coats and walk to the hall. The show is funny. On the way home, they talk about the best part and laugh again.

title: The Fish and the Leaf
text: A leaf falls into a pond. A fish swims under it. The leaf moves with the water. The fish moves too. A boy by the pond thinks the fish is playing. The leaf goes to the far side. The fish turns and swims home.

title: The Night Light
text: A little light lives by the bed. It is on only at night. A girl says, "I cannot sleep." The light shines on her book. She reads one page, then another. Soon her eyes close. The light stays on until the sun comes in.

title: The Quiet Room
text: The house is very quiet. Where is the cat? May looks in the kitchen and under the table. No cat. She hears a soft sound from a box. She opens it. The cat is asleep inside. May closes the box a little and lets it rest.

title: The Last Boat
text: The last boat is at the river. Kim runs to it with her bag. A man on the boat sees her and waits. Kim gets on. The boat moves across the water. On the other side, her sister is waiting. Kim waves before the boat stops.

title: The Red Leaf
text: Mia sees a red leaf by her door. It is small and bright. She puts it in a book. At night, Mia opens the book again. The red leaf is still there. It looks like a little fire. Mia smiles. Autumn has come to her home.

title: A Squirrel in the Park
text: Ken walks in the park on a cool morning. A squirrel runs under a tree. It finds a brown nut and holds it in two small hands. Then it hides the nut near a rock. Ken walks on. The squirrel is getting ready for cold days.

title: Soup for a Cool Evening
text: The wind is cool after sunset. Hana cuts carrots, an onion, and a potato. She puts them in a pot with water. Soon, the kitchen smells warm and good. Her brother brings two bowls to the table. They eat the soup slowly and listen to the wind outside.

title: Lanterns by the River
text: A small town holds an autumn walk beside the river. People carry paper lanterns. The lights move across the dark water. Luis walks with his host family. No one needs to hurry. They stop on a bridge, share sweet cakes, and watch yellow leaves float below.

title: The Geese Above the Field
text: Sara hears a sound above the farm. She looks up and sees wild geese flying in a long V. They are moving toward warmer places. Her grandfather stops his work and watches, too. For one quiet minute, the whole field seems to point south with them.

title: The Note in the Acorn
text: Noah finds a large acorn on the library steps. A thin piece of paper is tied around it. The note says, “Look where summer ends.” He follows a path to the old garden. Under the last green tree, he finds a box of bookmarks for the town's autumn reading club.

title: The Last Outdoor Table
text: Aiko likes to read at the cafe's outdoor table. In summer, every table is full. Now the mornings are cooler, and she is often alone. The owner brings her tea and a small blanket. Aiko reads while leaves cross the empty street. The quiet feels like a gift made only for her.

title: The Harvest Bell
text: For many years, a bell hung beside the village storehouse. Farmers rang it when the rice harvest was safely inside. The old storehouse is now a museum, but the bell still rings once each autumn. Children gather to hear it. Its clear sound connects today's town with the work of earlier families.

title: The Tree That Kept One Leaf
text: Every tree in the valley released its leaves except one ancient maple. It held a single golden leaf through wind and rain. A tired traveler slept beneath it. At dawn, the leaf fell into her hand and became a warm light. She carried it until she found the road home.

title: Why Leaves Change Color
text: Green leaves use a substance called chlorophyll to collect light. During shorter autumn days, many trees stop making as much of it. Other colors that were already in the leaves become easier to see. Yellow and orange appear, while some trees also produce red pigments. Weather and tree type affect the final display.

title: A Market at Harvest Time
text: At the mountain market, autumn arrives in baskets. Pears sit beside pumpkins, mushrooms, and late grapes. Yuna speaks with growers while steam rises from a soup stand. Each person describes the season differently: a color, a smell, a difficult week of rain. By noon, her bag holds food and many small stories.

title: The Keeper of the Seed Library
text: Mr. Alvarez manages a seed library in a small community center. Gardeners borrow seeds in spring and return new seeds after the autumn harvest. He carefully labels each envelope with its name and history. To him, the collection is more than a cabinet. It is a record of meals, gardens, and neighbors helping one another.

title: Footprints in the Orchard
text: After the apple harvest, Leila notices a line of footprints between the empty trees. They begin at the locked gate but do not return. She follows them to a damaged fence and finds a young deer caught in loose wire. The mystery becomes a rescue. By dusk, the animal is free, and the fence is safe again.

title: A Season Shared Differently
text: Autumn does not arrive everywhere at the same time or in the same way. While northern regions cool in September, places in the Southern Hemisphere are entering spring. Even within one country, mountains may change color before nearby coasts. Seasonal traditions therefore reflect local weather, crops, and history rather than a single universal calendar.

title: The Forest's Quiet Exchange
text: An autumn forest may appear to be closing down, yet it remains busy. Fallen leaves form a layer that shelters insects and holds moisture. Fungi and other decomposers gradually break the material apart, returning nutrients to the soil. What looks like an ending is also a transfer, as one season prepares the ground for another.

title: Reading by the Earlier Window
text: In June, Daniel could read beside the window until late evening. By October, darkness arrived before he finished work. At first he resented the shorter light. Then he moved a chair beneath a warm lamp and began a new ritual: twenty quiet minutes with a book before dinner. The changing season reshaped, rather than ended, his reading time.

title: How Communities Marked the Harvest
text: Harvest celebrations developed in many farming communities because gathering crops was both essential and uncertain. Their forms differed widely, shaped by local foods, beliefs, and labor. Shared meals, music, offerings, and public thanks could recognize the work of growers and the risks of weather. Modern festivals often preserve selected parts of these older seasonal practices.

title: Balance at the Equinox
text: The word equinox suggests equal night, but daylight and darkness are not exactly twelve hours everywhere on that date. The Sun is a disk rather than a point, and Earth's atmosphere bends its light. Sunrise is defined by the first visible edge of the Sun, while sunset uses the last edge. Together, these effects make daylight slightly longer.

title: Autumn at the Old Estate
text: When Elena returned to the estate, the garden had lost the strict order she remembered. Vines crossed the stone paths, and rain had darkened the statues. Yet the neglected place no longer seemed ruined. In the amber afternoon, every fallen leaf softened an old boundary. She understood that preservation did not always mean preventing change; sometimes it meant noticing what change revealed.

title: The Translator's Autumn Notebook
text: Each autumn, a retired translator reread one page from every book she had helped bring into another language. She did not search for errors. Instead, she marked decisions she would make differently now. The notebook became a record of changing judgment: words once defended, rhythms later questioned, and cultural details that experience had taught her to hear more clearly.
